## A100 vs H100: when the older card wins

The H100's biggest lead is on FP8 work, and the A100 has no FP8 support or Transformer Engine. On Beam, an H100 PCIe machine costs $1.83/hr against $1.36/hr for the A100 80GB SXM4, about 35% more, so the H100 only wins per job if it runs more than 1.35 times faster. Compute-bound training often does. Low-batch LLM inference in BF16 often doesn't, because the H100 PCIe's memory bandwidth is close to the A100 SXM4's. Our H100 PCIe price comparison covers the other side.

results.title: An inference cluster running four H100s at full tilt costs $10.28 an hour. The same traffic served through a mixed setup costs $4.01 an hour, with the same tokens going out the … | Spheron Network
results.author: Spheron Network
highlights:
# An inference cluster running four H100s at full tilt costs $10.28 an hour. The same traffic served through a mixed setup costs $4.01 an hour, with the same tokens going out the … | Spheron Network · LinkedIn · 2026-09-30T00:00:00+00:00

**Spheron Network**.

---

An inference cluster running four H100s at full tilt costs $10.28 an hour. The same traffic served through a mixed setup costs $4.01 an hour, with the same tokens going out the door.

Every request has two stages. Prefill reads your prompt and builds the first output token. Decode generates every token after that, one at a time. On a 512-token response, decode eats about 80% of the wall clock.

Decode is memory-bound, not compute-bound. The GPU spends most of its time moving data rather than doing math, so a cheaper card barely loses ground there.

Split the work by stage:
- Prefill runs on the H100, where raw compute reads the prompt fast
- Decode runs on the L40S, which serves tokens for far less per hour

The full numbers: 4x H100 runs $10.28/hr at $0.89 per million tokens. A mixed cluster of 1x H100 plus 2x L40S runs $4.01/hr at $0.46 per million tokens. That is a 61% cut in hourly spend and about 48% cut in cost per token.

We wrote up the setup: vLLM 0.8+ with NVIDIA Dynamo 1.0 routing requests between the two chip types.

highlights:
H100 FP8 spot costs $0.99, a fraction of that price.

...

**Spheron Network**.

---

B200 on-demand costs $6.03 an hour. H100 FP8 spot costs $0.99, a fraction of that price. On sticker price alone, H100 looks like the deal. It still does once you account for throughput.

The hourly rate ignores how much work each GPU finishes in that hour. FP8 and FP4 are number formats a GPU computes in. FP4 uses fewer bits per number than FP8, so it moves less data and processes more tokens per second.

MLPerf is an independent benchmark, not a Spheron-run test, and its numbers are the best available proxy for real throughput. On MLPerf v4.1, H100 FP8 spot produces 24,525 tokens per second. On MLPerf v5.1, B200 FP4 produces 102,725, about 4.2 times more.

Normalize price for that throughput gap and the ranking holds:

- H100 FP8 spot: about $0.090 per million tokens
- B200 FP4, on-demand: about $0.130 per million tokens

H100 still costs less per million tokens, even running at a fraction of B200 FP4's throughput. These figures come from Spheron's own FP4 quantization benchmark post and may shift as pricing and benchmarks update.

results.title: $0.89 to fine-tune Llama 3.1 8B on an H100. $1.35 for the identical job on an MI300X. | Spheron Network
results.author: Spheron Network
highlights:
# $0.89 to fine-tune Llama 3.1 8B on an H100. $1.35 for the identical job on an MI300X. | Spheron Network · LinkedIn · 2026-10-02T00:00:00+00:00

**Spheron Network**.

---

$0.89 to fine-tune Llama 3.1 8B on an H100. $1.35 for the identical job on an MI300X.

The GPU with more memory and the cheaper hourly rate still lost.

MI300X looks like the obvious pick. It has 192GB of memory, more than double the H100's 80GB, and a lower price per hour. On paper, it is the easy win.

Price per hour is not the bill. The bill is price per hour multiplied by wall-clock time, the real minutes a job takes to finish, not the hours you rent the card for.

We ran the same fine-tune on both cards: Llama 3.1 8B, trained with LoRA. LoRA trains a small set of added weights instead of the whole model. That takes less memory and less time than a full fine-tune.

H100 finished in 18 minutes. MI300X took 34 minutes, almost double.

The final cost follows the clock, not the specs:

- H100: $0.89 total
- MI300X: $1.35 total, 51% more

That does not make MI300X wrong everywhere. If your model does not fit in the H100's 80GB, the extra memory still matters more than speed. For a job that fits on both cards, the bigger memory and cheaper rate still pointed the wrong way.

These figures come from our own benchmark, run in September 2026. Pricing and results may shift by region and availability. Full benchmark

results.title: H100 Rental Prices Jump 22% in a Month as GPU Shortage Hits Firms and Labs - Seoul Economic Daily
results.author: An Hye-ji, Intern Reporter
highlights: - Key summary: Vessl AI, a domestic neocloud company, raised the hourly rate for Nvidia H100 chips on its VESSL Cloud service to $2.98 from $2.39 on the 1st of this month, a 24.7% increase. The price adjustment marks the start of similar moves in Korea after U.S. neocloud firms including CoreWeave and Nebius successively raised GPU rental rates. Vessl AI procures most of its roughly 7,000 GPUs through leasing. According to Ornn, an AI computing trading platform, the hourly cloud rental rate for the H100 rose 21.9% over the past month to $3.28 from $2.69, reaching about 70% of the price of the higher-end H200. The impact is spreading to industry and research, with some companies abandoning bids for government-led AI transformation projects because they could not secure GPUs, while universities and research institutes scale back the size of their research.
